subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup policy should OpenClaw use when active exec SecretRefs fail under a supervisor restart loop?
rationale: The current behavior is documented fail-fast startup, but this report shows a security-sensitive external rate-limit amplification; choosing retry, degraded startup, circuit breaking, config surface, or plugin-only delegation needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Generic bounded startup policy
options.body: Add a provider-agnostic bounded retry/backoff and operator-visible diagnostic path for startup SecretRef failures without hardcoding 1Password behavior in core.

options.title: Configurable circuit/cache design
options.body: Design a broader `secrets` policy surface for retry, circuit breaking, and delegated or persistent caching, accepting the extra config and migration review cost.

options.title: Plugin/delegated resolver only
options.body: Keep core fail-fast and document shared external resolvers such as the Varlock 1Password plugin for batching and caching, with no core startup behavior change.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup policy
recommendation.body: Add a provider-agnostic bounded retry/backoff and operator-visible diagnostic path for startup SecretRef failures without hardcoding 1Password behavior in core.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for provider-based external secrets and eager startup SecretRef activation points to joshavant.
